ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Wilma Mankiller

code.originalText: Two-week review with the neuromuscular neurology consultation the same day: antibody, nerve stimulation, chest CT and kidney ultrasound results, the diagnosis, and the treatment plan

text.paragraph: Two-week review: antibody, nerve stimulation and imaging results; neuromuscular neurology seen today. [S]

Ms. Mankiller returns two weeks after her first visit. On pyridostigmine 30 mg three times daily her eyelids lift for two to three hours after each dose, but double vision returns by evening and her arms still tire when she brushes her hair; she has mild stomach cramps and looser stools after doses. She has had no breathlessness, choking or weak cough. The acetylcholine receptor antibody test is strongly positive. The chest CT and kidney ultrasound were done last week. This morning she saw Dr. Okafor-Delaney of neuromuscular neurology, whose nerve stimulation test showed the typical decrement, and they agreed a plan: a higher pyridostigmine dose, prednisone started low and raised slowly, azathioprine once the screening tests are back, and an assessment for thymectomy. She asked that her blood tests be drawn near home where possible, and wants to understand each medicine before she takes it. She says the polycystic kidney disease is not new to her. [S]

list.item:
Generalized myasthenia gravis, AChR antibody positive, MGFA class IIa (G70.00). The diagnosis is confirmed by the antibody and the nerve stimulation decrement; MuSK antibodies and single-fiber EMG are not needed. No thymoma. FVC 3.25 L and negative inspiratory force -68 cm H2O: no sign of impending crisis. [S]
Pyridostigmine 60 mg four times daily while awake, before meals.
Prednisone 10 mg each morning, raised by 10 mg each week to 40 mg.
Azathioprine after TPMT activity and hepatitis B and tuberculosis screening, drawn today.
Thoracic surgery assessment for robotic thymectomy once stable.
Crisis warning signs and the list of medicines to avoid reviewed again.

Starting glucocorticoids (Z79.52). Baseline hemoglobin A1c 5.3 percent, blood pressure 124/80 mm Hg, weight 61.6 kg; a slow start lowers the risk of early worsening. [S]
Calcium carbonate 1250 mg and cholecalciferol 1000 units daily.
DXA at the next visit.
Glucose, blood pressure and weight at each visit.

Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (Q61.2). Both kidneys enlarged with many cysts; height-adjusted total kidney volume 364 mL/m at 34, Mayo Imaging Class 1B, not rapidly progressive, so tolvaptan is not indicated. eGFR 102 and urine albumin 14 mg/g at the first visit; blood pressure normal-high. [S]
Home blood pressure readings twice a week; target 110/75 mm Hg or lower if readings exceed 130/85.
Water 2 to 3 liters a day; less salt; no NSAIDs.
eGFR and urine albumin yearly.

Follow-up: Neuromuscular neurology nurse call in one week as prednisone rises. Thoracic surgery assessment in about four weeks. Review here in six weeks with blood count, chemistry, FVC and DXA. Next scheduled visit 2026-05-04: six-week review on pyridostigmine and prednisone: strength, breathing, glucose and blood pressure, bone density, start of azathioprine, and the thymectomy plan. [S]
